assessmentSummary.identity: A static bilateral high-compression hold in straight-arm push support. Both extended legs are held clearly above horizontal in the declared together or straddle position. Support implement, stable versus ring support, leg position, exact angle, assistance, hold time, and entry or exit are controlled variant or delivery dimensions.
currentCardFindings: No exercise card existed; formal FIG/USAG V-sit skill cards already exist and retain their proficiency classifications in the skill library.
The exercise identity begins when the declared extended-leg position is clearly above horizontal; a horizontal L position remains an L-sit rather than an unsuccessful V-sit.
Together and straddle versions preserve high straight-arm support compression but materially change hip-abduction range, flexibility interaction, symmetry, and difficulty.
Ring support preserves the V position but materially changes grip, stability, supervision, mount, exit, fatigue, and failure consequences and is an explicit variant.
Support height, exact V angle, assistance, hold time, and rest are modifiers when the above-horizontal static support identity remains unchanged.
Manna changes hip height and carries the legs beyond the shoulder line, materially changing shoulder, trunk, flexibility, balance, and assistance demands; it is a separate definition.
Exercise difficulty is complexity plus physical difficulty only, with overall equal to their maximum; formal proficiency belongs to skill-library cards.
All five media links remain candidate-only and require exact-match, safety, claim, caption, accessibility, and reviewer approval.

variantDifficultyCandidates.basis: Together-leg V-sit combines high-range bilateral compression with straight-arm support, balance, breathing, and controlled entry and exit.
Straddle may change the lever but adds hip-abduction range, adductor control, spatial organization, symmetry, and strict height classification.
Independent rings add grip, support stability, coordination, supervision, mount, exit, fatigue, and failure-consequence demands.

proposedLoadProfile.recoveryHours: Count the work with L-sit, Manna, presses, dips, ring support, hand support, active compression, hip-flexor, and long-lever trunk work. Ring support, long holds, high total time, or near-failure attempts warrant more recovery.

proposedDeliveryProfiles.dose: Two to five sets of three to ten clean seconds on stable support, or two to six seconds on rings, with 120 to 300 seconds rest and at least two seconds of visible quality reserve.
proposedDeliveryProfiles.qualityGate: Stable support, straight elbows, owned shoulder position, both feet clearly above horizontal, declared leg position, breathing, and controlled exit.

athlete: Push down and keep the elbows long.
Lift both extended legs clearly above horizontal.
Hold the selected together or straddle position while breathing.
Exit before height, support, or knee position changes.
coach: Declare support, leg position, minimum height, assistance, hold time, and exit before the set.
Observe hand contact, elbow and shoulder position, pelvis, knee angle, leg height, symmetry, breathing, and exit.
Classify a below-horizontal hold as L-sit work rather than crediting V-sit.
Count ring support separately in grip, stability, supervision, and recovery budgets.

proposedProgramming.sequence: Use after wrist, shoulder, support, and compression preparation while the athlete is fresh; place before fatiguing pressing, ring, hip-flexion, and high-volume trunk work.

athleteQuestions: Were both feet clearly above horizontal?
Did elbows and shoulders stay in the selected position?
Could you breathe and exit with reserve?
coachQuestions: Did support, height, knee position, symmetry, breathing, or exit limit first?
Was the hold actually V-sit or an L-sit fallback?
Does the next exercise share support, ring, or compression fatigue?

currentCardSnapshot.description: From a stable straight-arm push support on the floor, parallettes, dip bars, parallel bars, or rings, hold both extended legs clearly above horizontal while maintaining active shoulders, trunk and pelvic control, breathing, and a safe exit.

population.clinicalBoundary: Symptoms, recent surgery, instability, neurologic signs, or rehabilitation restrictions require individualized clinician guidance.

evidence.sourceTitle: Youth Resistance Training: Updated Position Statement Paper From the NSCA
claims: Resistance exercise selection requires qualified instruction, safe equipment and space, appropriate progression, and readiness assessed for the individual rather than inferred from an exercise label.

Before V-Sit, check the exact support, floor area, clearance, selected position, assistance, fatigue state, and exit. Stop for pain or pinching; numbness or tingling; dizziness; instability; support or hand slip; uncontrolled cramping; elbow or shoulder collapse; repeated loss of the declared trunk, knee, leg-height, range, breathing, or assistance standard; or an unsafe exit.

evidence.sourceTitle: Youth Training and Long-Term Athletic Development
claims: Training should be individualized and progressively developed from current readiness and movement competence.

Scale V-Sit with a shorter lever, smaller owned range, stable higher support, shorter sets or holds, more rest, declared assistance, plain-language cues, visual markers, or a mechanically appropriate substitute. Exercise cards use complexity and physical-difficulty scores; formal proficiency levels remain on skill-library cards.

evidence.sourceTitle: FIG Men's Artistic Gymnastics Code of Points 2025–2028
claims: The current governing-body code lists V-sit as a distinct held floor element and separates it from L-sit and Manna.
For exercise identity, require a static straight-arm support position with both extended legs clearly above horizontal; a horizontal position remains L-sit work.
The professional progression describes V-sit as an L-sit-derived support position with the legs raised substantially above horizontal and a changed lean and shoulder relationship.
Taxonomy should retain straight-arm push support and brace while explicitly recording above-horizontal leg position and together, straddle, or ring-support variants.

evidence.sourceTitle: Abdominal and hip flexor muscle activation during various training exercises
evidence.sourcePublisher: European Journal of Applied Physiology and Occupational Physiology
claims: Hip-flexion exercise can involve high hip-flexor activation with abdominal contribution.
For V-sit, combine hip-flexor, abdominal, quadriceps, triceps, scapular, shoulder-stabilizer, and hand/wrist support roles without claiming one isolated muscle causes the position.
Raising the legs above horizontal requires increased compression and a changed body and shoulder relationship compared with L-sit.
The position depends on active support, high hip flexion, knee extension, trunk and pelvic control, balance, and sufficient owned range rather than passive flexibility alone.

evidence.sourceTitle: FIG Men's Artistic Gymnastics Code of Points 2025–2028
claims: The governing-body code distinguishes held V-sit from L-sit and Manna and assigns them separate element boxes and values.

Candidate exercise difficulty is high because of above-horizontal compression, straight-arm support, balance, range, and exit demands; overall is max(complexity, physical difficulty), not the governing-body element value.
V-sit requires intense compression and substantial triceps and support demand.
Count V-sit with L-sit, Manna, presses, dips, ring support, hip-flexor, and high-compression work; stop before height, elbow, shoulder, knee, breathing, or exit quality changes.

evidence.sourceTitle: Youth Resistance Training: Updated Position Statement Paper From the NSCA
claims: Safe resistance exercise requires qualified instruction, appropriate progression, safe equipment and space, and individual readiness.
Require stable support, clear leg and exit space, pain-free support and high-compression range, an owned L-sit prerequisite, and direct observation.
Professional instruction treats V-sit as a high-demand progression built from shorter supported positions rather than a fatigue test.
Use short clean holds with full recovery and a visible quality reserve; cap attempts before position or support deteriorates.
The progression emphasizes a high tuck, straightening the legs, and eventually moving from L-sit into V-sit.
Cue stable support, straight elbows, active shoulders, clearly above-horizontal extended legs, declared together or straddle position, breathing, and a controlled exit.

evidence.sourceTitle: Basics of Strength and Conditioning Manual
claims: Exercise order, rest, volume, and progression should preserve the intended technique and adaptation.
Place V-sit while support and compression are fresh; budget hand, wrist, elbow, shoulder, hip-flexor, hamstring-range, trunk, and ring-stability demand.

evidence.sourceTitle: Youth Training and Long-Term Athletic Development
claims: Development should be individualized from current readiness and movement competence.
Give plain-language checks for stable support, straight elbows, shoulder height, feet clearly above horizontal, unchanged knee position, breathing, and early exit.

evidence.sourceTitle: Youth Resistance Training: Updated Position Statement Paper From the NSCA
claims: Qualified instruction and progression are central to safe youth resistance exercise.
The coach should declare the exact height standard, leg position, support, assistance, dose, and exit; distinguish V-sit from L-sit fallback; and regress before failure.

evidence.sourceTitle: FIG Men's Artistic Gymnastics Code of Points 2025–2028
claims: The code separates V-sit, Manna, and V-sit-to-handstand combinations as distinct held or combined elements.
Treat straddle and ring support as variants, exact angle and assistance as modifiers, L-sit and Manna as separate definitions, and press-to-handstand combinations as separate dynamic identities.

alternateAssessments.name: L-Sit
alternateAssessments.rationale: A horizontal extended-leg support hold does not meet the above-horizontal V-sit identity and has materially lower range and balance demand.

alternateAssessments.name: Straddle V-Sit
alternateAssessments.rationale: Straddle preserves the high support hold but changes hip-abduction range, adductor control, symmetry, and spatial organization.

alternateAssessments.name: Ring-Support V-Sit
alternateAssessments.rationale: Rings preserve the position while materially increasing grip, stability, supervision, mount, exit, and recovery demands.

alternateAssessments.name: Assisted V-Sit
alternateAssessments.rationale: Declared safe assistance changes external support and dose without changing the target V position; assistance method and amount must be recorded.

alternateAssessments.name: Higher-Angle V-Sit
alternateAssessments.rationale: Increasing an already above-horizontal owned angle changes range and difficulty within the same identity until the hip and leg relationship crosses into Manna.

alternateAssessments.name: V-Sit to Handstand Press
alternateAssessments.rationale: Adding a dynamic press to inverted support changes primary action, movement pattern, phase, risk, prerequisites, and dosage.

alternateAssessments.name: Manna Hold
alternateAssessments.rationale: Manna elevates the hips and carries the legs beyond the shoulder line, changing shoulder extension, trunk, flexibility, balance, assistance, and exit demands.

alternateAssessments.name: V-Up
alternateAssessments.rationale: V-up is a dynamic supine trunk-and-hip flexion repetition without straight-arm push support.
